recs.name: One Packed Daily Schedule
recs.tag: Every day's non-stop, round the clock. There's bad times, there's good times.

lines.x: Rhodes Island Landship
'Lutra Workshop'
Ooh, looks like it's about time. Gotta get to work now.
Lemme see the schedule for today.
Mmm...
Mmyeah, works for me.
Let's get around to Maggy's 'Improvement proposals for Drone Dragonfly operation' and polish off my submissions for today. Get around to the rest later. Then I just gotta wait for her.
Doing maintenance on Saria's armor? Main thing should be giving it a new coat of paint... crap, did I not order paint?!
Arghh—we're good, we're good. Didn't use it up last time.
Main focus for today'll be that.
If I get the time, I'll send some orders for a couple new parts. Then I can give all my frontline Meeboos some real maintenance.
Mm-hm. Today's lineup, sorted.
Let's kick it off!
Mayer!
Mayer, open the door!
It's urgent!
Not too happy about Saria's suit here...
Wonder why it can't charge up properly.
Weird. C'mon, where's the problem, officer?
Mayer! I know you're in there!
I hear you talking!
Rooound here?
Ah-hah~ Gotcha.
Prime suspect found. We're on Easy Street now.
Don't make me do it!
Just need to restore a failed node, and the whole suit should be back up and working again.
Uh-huh. Optimize charge circuits first. Paint over next. You'll be back to regular service in no time.
D'you want some extra features while I'm at it? Hmm.
Ugh. I don't know if Kal'tsit's gonna chew me out for abusing privileges...
Who cares. Your fault for acting deaf, Mayer.
Mayer!
Settled.
Check over your nodes one more time. Gonna be a pain once the paint gets all in you.
Working with earphones in? Aren't you worried someone's gonna spook you?
Mmm...
Hm-hmm—
(Claps Mayer's shoulder)
(Opens mouth and bites)
Waaagghahagh!!!
Ow, ow!
Let go of me, damnit, let go of me!!
I'm a BAD meal!
You really blew it, Mayer. I had something good for you, and you wouldn't even open the door for me. Plus, you bit me...
Sorry, Closure. But, like, you know I bite when someone interrupts my work.
Owwieeee.
Fine, I'll let you bite me too, then. Fair's fair?
You're applying anti-Originium paint to a suit right now, I see?
Sure am.
Pass, then. I bite you here and one moment later I'll be in Medical. Not worth it.
Eh, I guess you're not wrong.
Mmm...
Closure?
What's up?
The door's stuck open.
I specifically remember setting it up to automatically open and close. Pretty sure I also set it a moment ago to 'do not disturb.'
Did you just hack my door?
Uhh—
No way~~ It was like that when I walked in.
Your door just wasn't locked.
Didn't I lock it?
...Weird.
Can you gimme a moment? I'll check the tapes.
You put a camera up?!
I got a lotta sensitive Rhine material in here, y'know? It'd be bad news for all of us if I lost something.
Gotta take basic security measures.
Nah, you should get back to work for now...
R—Remember your health and safety regs. This paint's, uh, pretty dangerous, yeah? Things could go wrong with you trying to multitask!
It's fine, I've got mechanical arms on it.
Hmm, which program was it again?
Er, Mayer, don't you think this paint's gonna go volatile soon?
That paint? It's fine, sheesh. It's inert.
You could dump it in boiling water and ionize it for three hours, freeze it, and it'd still be good to go the moment it thaws.
Is this the folder?
OK, monitor program, on.
Time seek to—
Mayer!
Let's make smart robots together!
Mayer?
M—Mayer?
What did you just say?
Could—Could you repeat that?
Make some smart robots with me?
Sure!
Then let's work specifics somewh—
(Presses monitor feed transmission toggle)
Bzzzz—
(Sound of door opening)
Ugh. I don't know if Kal'tsit's gonna chew me out for abusing privileges...
Who cares. Your fault for acting deaf, Mayer.
Meeboos.
Get her ass.
AaaaghhI'msorryit'smyfault don't sic the Meeboos on me ow ow ow ow waaaghhhhh!!!
Yeah, go on. What was it you wanted me for?
Uwaaahh...
I wanted you to help me with an explosive-type thingy...
Underlying machine's a Raythean Challenger Hellcat high-performance operation platform...
Topside already has a custom-ordered full-thermal Arts impact generator...
But it's not working a hundred percent perfect, so I need your help...
Uwaaahh...
Yeah, okay.
Just take a sniff of this first.
Okaaaayhhh...
(Inhale)
I know this!
(Takes a deep breath)
You better now?
Hahhhh~~~~
Better!
Eheheheh. Thanks, Mayer.
We're not gonna get any business done with you bawling your eyes out.
True that, heheh.
Still dunno why you love sniffing the refined lubricant I have in here...
Well, 'cause it smells good, duh.
Guess Warfarin wasn't wrong. There's no blood in your veins, just machine oil.
Enough of that. Let's get real.
Aye-aye.
You need me to refit the Raythean Challenger. Raise its attack power. Right?
Also, self-defense, damage resist, and evac plans. After all, we're gonna put a smart little guy in there. Can't have it breaking after one use.
Then you came to the right person.
Now. My reward?
Remember how there was a little hoard in the hangar? As long as you—
I'll take the job!
Heheh. Let's get along, partner.
Gettin' along, gettin' along~
But, uh.
What?
See the blackboard over there?
Covered in sticky notes?
Yeah.
That's my schedule.
Even if as a rush job, your commission still lands bottom-right of the very last note.
Uhh—
Any way I can jump the queue?
No, sirree.
So in other words, two months.
Work fast, it'll be fifty days.
Huh?
Do you really work that fast?!
Decently. Sometimes inspiration hits and the work's done.
Er... I'll leave you to it, then...
Good luck with work!
Hold it!
Huh?
You format the door for me first. I need to do its settings over.
Also, strip your sys-op authority off it.
Right now. Straight away. Giddy up.
Uhh—
Awright...
Two hours later...
Just the laaast bit—
Ding dong!
Mayer, it's me.
Um...
Did you change the password? Is that why the door's not opening?
And that should be about done.
Huh? Someone at the door again?
It's me!
Maggy! The door's broken! Push the button on the side and come in!
Hi, you.
Heyo.
I'm still busy with something for Saria here. Can't lay out the carpet for you.
So, you need something from me?
I made a reservation.
Drone plans. Wondering how they're doing?
Huh... oh!
That. Already done.

Listed out some technical essentials, improvement proposals and required materials. Everything's in that file on the table there. You look through, and if it's all good, we can set up a new time to help you make some fitting parts.
If you've got issues with it, we'll have a meeting about it.
Rightie. Thanks, Mayer.
Which file on which table is it?
That one, that one.
Your mechanical arms are pointing at at least four different tables. How should I know which one?
Mayeeer—
Ahhh don't pull me! I'm still painting here!
You can leave paint and keep painting later. Help me find the files first, okay?
Mayeeeer~~
I get it.
Mm-hm. Thankies~
Mmn—it's this one.
Oh...
These are your expensed items for last month.
Oh, sorry. I meant this one.
Mmm...
Yep, that's it!
Thank you, Mayer!
Ain't no thang. Just what I oughta do.
Then I'll be heading out now. Bye-bye.
Ah.
I almost forgot the most important part!
Can I ask you what the time is right now?
Noon, right?
Afternoon already!
Mayer, have you eaten yet?
Huh? You mean me? I eat an energy bar and I'm fine.
That's no good!
Here, take this!
This is?
I bought it at the cafeteria. They had the freshwater stuff you love today.
I wanted you to come eat with me, but then I lost track of time myself...
So after I finished eating, I got a portion bagged up to bring over.
Ooh, thanks.
Make sure you eat it.
Mm-hm, I will.
Anything else?
Is this Saria's Charged Suit?
That it is.
How much longer will you be working?
An hour or two-ish.
Well, that's no good. Let me help you out there.
It's fine, I can do it.
Either you let me help you, or I feed you your meal. Pick one.
Ugh...
Alright fine I get it! Give me a hand.
Hehe~
Then let's get to work~
Phew. We're done.
Good work.
C'mere and wash your hands.
Alright—
*Sigh*... It's only times like these I miss all of Rhine's self-cleaning facilities.
So why don't you go back?
If I went back, they'd set me up with a mountain of annoying work, and I'd have no time to improve my Meeboos.
And, like, I had to deal with interpersonal stuff there too.
Like you don't have to here?
You're always out on fieldwork. You don't know all the politics and warring between sections.
Over there, right? You'd make a new friend one day, turn around, and bam, someone tells you 'they're from the blah-blah section, best you stay away from them.'
And what's worse is even if you're in the same section, sometimes your bosses are competing and you're all trying to drag each other down.
That's stuff I'm, like, just not good at dealing with.
So I ended up scarpering here.
I see...
Sorry, I shouldn't have asked you about...
It's okay...
Alright, let's eat.
Then I should be on my way.
Meeboos, can I ask you to keep an eye on her? Otherwise she'll go straight back to work the moment I'm gone.
My Meeboos don't have voice modules. They won't answer you.
I still have to nag you.
Okay then. This time I'm really off. Bye-bye.
Bye bye.
Hmm, maybe I should put those part orders through before I eat—
Whuah! What the hell are you doing, Meeboos?!
It's just a little bit of work. I'm not gonna forget to eat.
Ugh...
Fine, I get it, I'm eating, I'm eating now!
Phew, I'm stuffed. Alright, work!
Mmm, order parts first or fix some Meeboos first?
Meeboos win out, yeah. Meeboos are more important.
C'mere.
Lemme see—
Touch up paint, inspect wiring, update data, replenish energy.
That's what Meeboo maintenance is made of...
Better!
Still four more on mission duty, and my five reserve ones need servicing too.
What time is it, again?
Looks like I can get 'em done today.
Mmm...
Probably. Probably can.
As long as nobody else—
Mayer! Open up!! Work needs you!
Oh, c'mon, for fffff~!@~#!@...
*Huff*, *huff*.
Stay cool.
In—out, in—out.
Smile~
Alright.
Whoa, so you're in.
What's got you all smiles and rainbows?
You come here. I'll tell you.
Sure—
See? This is a Meeboo.
I know.
Stick your hand out. It's got something good for you.
Huh, don't hear that every day. Wonder what it is?
Meeboo, get his ass.
Aaaaarggh-don't-bite-me-ow-ow-ow-ow-ow!!!
Late night
Ahhh—finally.
All done!
Everything I planned this morning is all done!
Ahh—that doesn't count. I made the executive decision just now to move ordering parts to tomorrow.
Lemme see what I gotta do tomorrow.
Go to the Procurement Department and order parts.
Need to install test equipment for Medical.
Oh, gotta debug my workbench again.
That should settle tomorrow's lineup.
Time is... 11:36.
Mm, yeah, I should crash.
Eat a bowl of instant noodles and then sleep.
See you tomorrow, Meeboos.
Agh—ow, ow!

recs.name: Heart of Creation
recs.tag: From Rhine Lab to Rhodes Island, they've always come with.

lines.x: Rhodes Island Landship
'Lutra Workshop'
Don't blink now, Closure.
Meeboo SUPER, select M-11 Originium-Proof Coating from the table.
(There's a dozen types of coating here, and they all pretty much look and feel the same sans packaging.)
Got it in one.
C'mon, that's just basic stuff.
There's a broken component in this thermal sensor. Repair it in three minutes, Meeboo SUPER.
Repair complete. There is an electronic component under the base that compromises thermal sensor efficiency. It has been removed without affecting device operation.
Sweet! Took less than two!
Wow! It talks!
What's a smart upgrade without a voice module?
Took some time to get used to it myself. It's not exactly the chatty type, though.
Did you really have to make the voice so gruff though...? Whatever, to each their own.
Keep going.
Meeboo SUPER, set a new password for the workshop door.
Password set using a combination of alphanumeric characters in upper and lower cases, and special characters. Password does not include your birthday.
Alright, awesome!
Applied testing, phase one complete!
And there you have it, the new, the improved, the Meeboo SUPER! So? What'd ya think? Smarter than your AI buggies, right?
Sure is a clever little guy! But Lancet-2 or Castle-3 could do all that, no problem.
Hey, no biting! You're just like Mayer!
Let her go for now, Meeboo SUPER.
Can't tell if its performance is better than the buggies, but it sure holds a grudge better.
Stay away!
So, how much time did this upgrade take you?
Lemme see... three months, ish?
Closure, Closure! I've got that 'Raythean Challenger Hellcat Demon High-Performance Operation Platform' upgrade proposal you wanted!
Thanks. Next up is—
Nah, I need a month off.
Whoa, a workaholic like you? Burnt out? Or... are you looking for a raise?
No way, you know me.
Just finished up all my requests from Rhine Lab and Rhodes Island, so my schedule's a clear blue sky.
And it's high time I upgraded the Meeboos.
Haven't you been doing that in your spare time? What do you need more time for all of a sudden?
Three more Meeboos have gone kaput the last few months, and there's still a whole pile waiting for repair.
There's only one 1st-gen left.
Aw, poor little guys.
Their efficiency's improved, but survival rate remains poor in adverse environments, or operations requiring a high degree of precision.
Implementing a full AI should let 'em properly take care of themselves while performing their tasks.
Oh, I'll help then!
Thanks, but no thanks. I'll be fine on my own.
Why not? Didn't we work together on Iwona's Justice Knight?
That was a PRTS-based customization. Not even you know the ins and outs of the buggies' operational algorithms.
That's not what I want for my babies. From Rhine to Rhodes, I've always worked on 'em myself.
I'll give you a shout if I've got any questions, though.
I'd installed a learning system on 'em, but that's not even in the same ballpark as true 'intelligence.' Needed to start from scratch.
First I tried optimizing the existing Meeboo core to improve its automation logic, but the results weren't too great.
So I rewrote the underlying code... Which took a while.
Original plan called for five SUPER prototypes to get some proper control experiments in, but I only managed to finish one.
Still! This Meeboo SUPER is an unprecedented achievement with applications in highly complex environments, including demolition, surveying, reconnaissance, combat, and everyday life.
Most importantly, it can complete precise operations fully independently.
It'll be the most powerful smart machine in all Terra... Small and easy to mass produce too. Makes your customized buggies look like a science fair project.
We're talking about a whole Meeboo army!
So what's this tag on it?
Nametag. Got one on every Meeboo.
But why so many? Let's see, C00-1, B03-4, B12, G70...
Took 'em off of decommissioned Meeboos.
Yeah, I know, but weren't those supposed to go in the Great Meeboos Monument? Did you...
So the Meeboo SUPER carries on its brothers' hopes and dreams?
Hehe.
But you still left yourself control permissions for the Meeboo's core, yeah?
I guess.
Then it's not quite 'smart' enough, yet.
I'll start the next phase of applied testing in a couple days.
I'll see you then, then.
By the way, make sure you've got the settings right on the Meeboo SUPER's demolition program. We are on the landship, after all...
Now I just gotta log today's test data.
Hey, are you even listening, Mayer?
I know, I know.
Oh, right, what's the new door password, Meeboo SUPER?
Huh... Is that a bug?
Meeboo SUPER!

lines.st: Meeboo SUPER Test Logs 07
Continuing applied testing for the Meeboo SUPER prototype today.
I'll temporarily disable my control permissions for the Meeboo core, allowing the Meeboo SUPER to autonomously inspect nearby buildings and resolve potential problems.
This is the most important stage.
Meeboo has learned to speak, though we're both still getting used to it. It's learning to complete more complex tasks; it's no longer just a 'walking bomb.'
However, this is the first time ever that a Meeboo will be operating outside my control.

If successful, it will mean that the Meeboos have truly reached the stage of artificial intelligence, without relying on the Rhodes Island mainframe, which is very important for both Lutra Workshop and the Meeboos.
Although there have been some occasional data deviations, based on the Meeboo SUPER's performance to date, I think there's a lot to look forward to in today's testing.
After all, every last Meeboo is lending us their strength.

lines.x: Core control permission off.
Meeboo SUPER, scan and resolve potential issues for buildings in the designated area.
Of course, since we're on the Rhodes Island Landship, you'll need to...
Oh, what am I saying, you're smart, you know what to do, right? Haha.
Whew—
Now just gotta wait for it to finish the job and come back.
Wow, the requests sure have piled up... Guess I really put 'em off for too long.
Let's see... wall projectors for operator quarters, weapons system upgrade for the training grounds, synchronization between drones and charging equipment...
And the workshop's a mess.
Might as well clean up the operating console while I have time.
Meeboo— SUPER. Scanning building. Resolving potential problems. Scanning building. Resolving potential problems.
8 structural integrity issues found. Calculating. Issues resolved using method—
One remaining structure to inspect.
'Lutra Workshop'
There, that's more like it!
Full-area scan.
Retrieving comparison data. Activating analysis.
Results—
Area is larger than expected. Lacks distinction between living and working space. Presence of dangerous equipment—
Warning. Resolving potential issue. Evacuate area.
Now lemme fix these heat sensors.
Warning. Resolving potential issue. Evacuate area.
Running short on materials. Guess I'll need to submit another order to the Procurement Department...
Resolving issue using method— method—
Demolition.
Did something just move?
Mayer was not slow on the uptake, but she could have been faster if she had shaken the habit of working with her headphones on.
The Meeboo SUPER activates its detonation sequence.
Using an extendable robotic arm, Mayer manages to press the shock shield activation button just in time, deflecting the Meeboo SUPER's directional explosion.
Lutra Workshop's key areas were undamaged, but the extendable platform near the door holding heavy materials is destroyed.
Mayer watches as the Meeboo SUPER is buried in the rubble it created.
Argh!
So... heavy...! Good thing the robotic arm charging system still works.
Meeboo SUPER!
What's going on, Mayer? I could hear the noise from your workshop a mile away.
Whoa, the Meeboo SUPER... looks heavily damaged.
Did it do all this?
Can't say I blame it... I told you not to use your quarters as your workshop, and not to make unauthorized modifications. Lemme check if the load-bearing structure is still intact...
What about the other places it inspected? Did it...?
I came from that way. Things look okay.
(Good thing I set up those localized shock compensators ahead of time. Whew...)
How about you? You okay, Mayer?
Look at this mess. I'll help you clean up.
Just like the old days.
Huh?
The workshop's a mess... just like the old days.
Don't scare me like that! You hit your head or something? You're not the type to reminisce at the drop of a hat, are you?
I mean, back when I first started on the Meeboos...
Mayer's workshop again?
Third time this month, isn't it?
Chronometer stops working, cooling system malfunction... and now the chair springs up on its own and knocks the operating table over?
It's always one thing or another pulling her away from the project and back to her lab.
And all this after she was even given her own workshop...
If she says it's a coincidence, who are we to argue? Not worth wasting time worrying about.
I was so excited to get into Rhine Lab.
For researchers, it was the holy land for all of Columbia—all of Terra, even. It had the facilities, the projects, the talent, the pay, and the benefits.

We had a consensus that science would determine the future of Terra. Within Rhine Lab itself, however, everyone had their own interpretation of science, their own obsessions. Especially the directors.
It was an uncomfortable place. Some of the finest minds in the world, but woefully inefficient when they get together, like an all-star sports team that just can't seem to win.

I was in Engineering, providing technical support for the other sections. A project started by Energy last month, which was already halfway through preparations, was facing termination because of opposition from Control.
Similarly, the Defense Section could also put a stop to ongoing projects at their discretion.
This happened again and again at Rhine Lab. Low-level staff were in a constant cycle of installation, testing, and removal.
I felt like I was better off doing research on my own.

That's why I made a trick alarm clock that caused just a teensy bit of havoc in my workshop at preset times. Not enough to put the place out of commission, but serious enough that I'd have to rush back to deal with it.
That was the first Meeboo prototype.
I gradually added more functions, and named them after the boot-up sound.
So you'd run back to your lab, all excited to clean up the mess?
Yeah. Never made much progress on the projects they assigned me, but I sure invented plenty of little gizmos.
After I helped her out, Silence liked some of the stuff I made and put in a recommendation. They still use 'em back at Rhine Lab, even.
The Meeboos were always the apple of your eye, though, weren't they?
Yeah, I wanted 'em to become these crazy smart machines.
I mean, they've been by my side this whole time, from Rhine to Rhodes.
But after countless losses, decommissions, and upgrades... there was only one 1st-gen Meeboo left.
Meeboo SUPER...
Was built around the last 1st-gen, yeah.

lines.st: Meeboo SUPER Test Logs 08
Internal sensor nodes malfunctioned. Major and irreversible warping of the limbs.
89.7% of the core is damaged. Repair would be difficult. There appear to be preexisting algorithmic issues, which had already manifested with the door password error.
Meeboo SUPER had worked independently for one hour prior to returning to Lutra Workshop, which was enough to overload its processing.
It saw items that operators left outside their doors as structural issues and blew them up...
That's not smart at all.
Sigh...
Analysis: The Meeboo SUPER prototype is no longer suited for practical operation.
Damage to the workshop's walls, loss of material... repairs will cost a fair bit.
Conclusion: This Meeboo upgrade is a failure.

lines.x: Hey, no one said artificial intelligence was easy.
Don't let it get to you!
Mayer!
What?
The Meeboo SUPER may not have achieved its goals, but it wasn't a complete failure.
C'mon, we can all see what happened, Closure.
No, I'm serious, look!
The nametags of the Meeboos.
Yeah. Its limbs are all crushed and warped, but the nametags have just fallen off, completely intact.
It's not like they're made of anything tougher than the main body, are they?
Wait, are you saying it...?
Could be a coincidence, or it could be some sort of 'instinct'...
Meeboo SUPER...
The voice module is too damaged to respond.
Beautiful! You should've seen the looks on their faces when I ditched.
But I gotta scoot you over a little for next time. Knocking over a chair is one thing, but fixing broken equipment is a pain.
I should give you a name, huh... You know what, how about I set up a random boot-up sound for you? Whatever sound you make will be your new name!
Over here, Meeboo. I need to reset the settings for your demolition program.
Meeboo, adjust the position of the robotic arm.
Meeboo, bring me that thermal device.
Meeboo... Hey, how'd you know I wanted this calibrator?
Whoa! What are you doing? Stop pulling!
It's just a bit of work. Not like I'm gonna forget to eat.
Er...
Fine, I get it, I'm eating, I'm eating!

lines.st: Mayer picks up the name tags from the ground and wipes the dirt off them.
She does so carefully, like she is organizing experimental data or putting together a precision machine.
More carefully, in fact.
Mayer has developed many things: wire-controlled machines, energy coating, transmission systems... She has become numb to the joys of creation.
Is there surprise, excitement, pride? Yes.
But nothing too intense.
This is normal for a researcher. That is why she credits her achievements to the Lutra Workshop.
Even though she is the Lutra Workshop.
The Meeboos, however, were different.
She talked to them, worked with them, killed time with them, and brought them with her from Rhine Lab to Rhodes Island.
She asked them to respond, and they did.
Mayer gazes upon the remains of the Meeboo SUPER. It was, without a doubt, a failure, but Mayer feels something she had never felt before.
Sadness? Surprise? Joy? Yes.
But it is more than that. Stronger, more complex, harder to describe.

lines.x: So, not quite buggy tier yet, but Meeboo SUPER has made a lot of progress. Don't give up.
Can I get another two months off, then?
I want to start the next smart upgrade project based on these results! Strike while the iron is hot!
No way, buster! I'm not falling for that!
I already gave you three months. Do you realize how many requests Engineering gets in three months?
And you'll also need to submit a detailed report on what happened during the Meeboo SUPER's testing, especially the accident.
Ugh...
And most importantly, you're paying for the Lutra Workshop's repairs out of your own pocket!
Meeboo SUPER Test Logs 09
This Meeboo upgrade has failed.
But the Meeboos are by Mayer's side. The possibilities are infinite.
Mayer trusts Meeboo.
Mayer trusts Mayer.
